question.text: The tax considerations section of the PPM for Saraswati Tech Fund mentions pass-through tax status. What does this mean for Category I and II AIF investors?

answer.text: The AIF pays all taxes on behalf of investors, and investors receive tax-free returns
Income earned by the AIF is not taxed at the fund level but is taxed in the hands of investors based on their individual tax status, as per applicable pass-through provisions
The AIF and investors both pay tax on the same income, resulting in double taxation
Tax obligations are deferred until the investor exits the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: For Category I and II AIFs, tax pass-through gives zero tax liability at the investment-fund level for income other than business income; that income is taxed directly in the investors' hands according to their own tax status. The Trap: Business income earned by the AIF remains taxable at the fund level even for Category I/II, so pass-through is not absolute. Option A wrongly implies returns are tax-free, Option C invents double taxation, and Option D wrongly defers tax to exit. Note: Pass-through means the tax obligation flows to the investor — it does not eliminate tax — and the business-income carve-out is a key exception.
